ranked_facts.why: The lesion's gradual progression to the frontal scalp and formation of a linear furrow on the forehead is more characteristic of Linear or Annular Lupus Erythematosus Panniculitis of the Scalp (LALPS) than of Lupus Erythematosus Profundus, Discoid Lupus Erythematosus, or Lupus Panniculitis.

The positive direct immunofluorescence with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels is more consistent with Linear or Annular Lupus Erythematosus Panniculitis of the Scalp (LALPS) than with Lupus Erythematosus Profundus, Discoid Lupus Erythematosus, or Lupus Panniculitis.

The presence of granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels, as indicated by direct immunofluorescence, is more characteristic of Linear or Annular Lupus Erythematosus Panniculitis of the Scalp (LALPS) than of other conditions like Scarring Alopecia, Neoplastic Scalp Disease, Infectious Scalp Disease, or Other conditions.
